title: Writ Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for Issuance of Writ of Mandamus / Certiorari
whenToUse: Use when an individual or corporate citizen seeks judicial review before the High Court against arbitrary executive action, administrative inaction, or violation of Articles 14, 19, or 21.
variantComparisonNote: Originating constitutional writ petition under Article 226. Distinct from civil suit under Section 9 CPC and counter-affidavits.
youWillNeed: Impugned government order / rejection letter, representations submitted to authority, proof of postal dispatch, identity proof.
legalBasis: Article 226 of the Constitution of India; Whirlpool Corporation v. Registrar of Trade Marks (1998); Radha Krishan Industries v. State of H.P. (2021).
mandatoryStatutoryIngredients: Demonstration of Respondent as 'State' under Article 12 of the Constitution
Clear infringement of Fundamental Rights or statutory public duties
Averment of absence of an efficacious and speedy alternative remedy
Prior demand for justice / representation made to competent authority without result

particulars.label: Seat of High Court
particulars.description: Principal Bench or Circuit Bench city

particulars.label: Filing Date
particulars.description: Date of presentation before High Court

aiBlocks.title: Factual Narrative & Arbitrary Executive Action
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Narrate Petitioner's entitlement, arbitrary rejection/inaction by {{FACT:authority_respondent}}, breach of legitimate expectation, and violation of Articles 14 and 19(1)(g).

aiBlocks.title: Substantive Constitutional Grounds
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Formulate concise constitutional grounds demonstrating Wednesbury unreasonableness, breach of natural justice, discrimination, and absence of alternative remedy.

aiBlocks.title: Prayer for Prerogative Writ & Interim Stay
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Draft prayer for Writ of Certiorari quashing impugned decision, Writ of Mandamus directing statutory action, and ad-interim stay on adverse proceedings.
